790671001.text: You are here, my loyal Paladin. The gifts that I have prepared for you are in the chest next to us — please, take them.

790671003.text: Hmm... Well, first of all, I shall announce to the whole forest that the relic has made its decision.

790671004.text: As for the chosen Guardian... I will tell them that it was Mr. Faurobert, the one who came from afar.

790671005.text: Huh!? Why would you do that?

790671006.text: Trying to explain everything we've been through would be far too complicated.

790671007.text: Besides, it would take too long for them to grasp the concept of me being both a princess and a Guardian at the same time.

790671008.text: When the time is right, I will make a detailed record of all that happened and then inform my people in writing.

790671009.text: But until then, I will still preside over all the affairs of the forest as "Princess."

790671010.text: Once those "trial grounds" have been officially converted into "training grounds," I will set off.

790671013.text: I still don't have the answers though.

790671014.text: Why did we need to wait for a Guardian, why did all those kingdoms decline as a result, and why is Rainsong Pond's calling what it is...

790671015.text: There are still so many unanswered questions, so many unfinished stories.

790671016.text: Speaking of which, *sigh*... I have another question...

790670104.text: Oh, it's you! Such a relief that you've come...

790670105.text: Thank you for coming, my honorable Paladin. We seem to have run into a rather peculiar problem...

790670106.text: Peculiar problem? Oh no, don't tell Paimon that the relic hasn't acknowledged Mr. Faurobert either?

790670107.text: If the problem was only that I hadn't been acknowledged as Guardian, that would actually be simpler...

790670108.text: How to put this... Mr. Faurobert is indeed the champion jumper — that much is indisputable.

790670109.text: But the trial he passed was Rainsong Pond's jumping contest, and when he was acknowledged as champion, it was a committee that declared him so.

790670110.text: It is true that Her Highness resides in a tall tower, and that this kingdom does indeed have its own series of arduous trials...

790670111.text: But she clearly isn't trapped, much less needs me to jump up and rescue her.

790670112.text: And those trials... No matter how good I was at jumping, I'd never be able to pass them... They just aren't designed for paper frogs.

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the Cave of Eerie Murmurs

790670201.text: Didn't the princess take us to the Cave of Eerie Murmurs before?

790670202.text: Paimon's sure she heard a strange voice while we were there.

790670203.text: Uhm, just to let you guys know... Us paper frogs aren't very good at jumping in caves...

790670204.text: Don't worry, Mr. Faurobert! Paimon might've just been hearing things...

790670205.text: "...I am a voice, but a voice is not life..."

790670206.text: "...Interaction is only born of contradictions, and only interaction is dialogue..."

790670208.text: Do not fear, these voices will not harm us. They are simply lamenting their own past.

790670211.text: To be precise, both princesses and princes. What they have in common is... They are all voices from fallen kingdoms.

790670212.text: They came in search of answers, but found nothing. All they could do was stay and lament their fate in vain.

790670401.text: Lotus leaves and dewdrops, what the... Why has this story been carved on the wall?

790670403.text: Someone's carved a story here that goes: "Once upon a time, there was a paper frog who wished he had a pair of wings."

790670404.text: "He prayed to the goddess, who told him that if he could jump higher than all the other frogs, he would have his wings..."

790670405.text: Wait a sec... If he could already jump higher than all the other frogs, why would he need wings?

790670407.text: No... This champion's name is actually recorded in the committee's register.

790670408.text: This paper frog, whose name was Cibrelus, once won the championship seven times in a row. No frog was his equal.

790670409.text: His symbol was a pair of wings made of lotus leaves, so they dubbed him "Winged Cibrelus."

790670410.text: Seven times in a row... P—Paimon heard you won the championship many times in a row, too, Mr. Faurobert...

790670411.text: Me? Yes, I've won it seven times, and Estampe six.

790670412.text: But I'd be no match for this champion! Back in those days, they had to figure it all out themselves, without any experience to go on.

790670413.text: If my generation of frogs have jumped higher than others, it is merely by jumping up from the shoulders of giants...

790670414.text: There he goes again, putting himself down as usual...

790670415.text: So what happened to that champion?

790670416.text: This I do not know... According to the committee's records, in the last jumping contest he ever took part in, Cibrelus came second.

790670418.text: Indeed it does. Given that he no longer felt up to the task of rescuing the princess, Cibrelus... announced his retirement there and then.

790670419.text: He told his friend that the jumping contest no longer held any meaning for him, and that unless he rediscovered its meaning someday, he would never again compete.

790670420.text: From that day forth, not once was his name ever again mentioned in the records of Rainsong Pond.

790670421.text: ...So just like those princes and princesses, there was a point in time after which this champion simply vanished from the world.

790670422.text: That's right. *sigh* All in all, this story really doesn't seem like a promising omen...

790670423.text: Hold on a minute... The last line of this story is also: "Stories follow rules, unfolding in cyclical patterns, but each should follow its own course."

790670424.text: Why does this line keep reappearing...

790670425.text: We'd better complete the rest of the trials first.

790670426.text: Yes, you're right. Let's focus on the puzzle before us.

790670427.text: I wonder where it will lead us in the end...

790670429.text: Looks like this cave has no intention of just giving us the answers, but rather plans on testing us instead...

790670430.text: Hmm... The road to success is never straight, huh?

790670436.text: Thank you! Then let's... go take a look at this final trial!

790670433.text: I am truly sorry to put you through all this, my Paladin. But this is the last step... Please, lend us your strength.

790670434.text: Paimon's so exhausted she feels like she can barely float...

790670435.text: #But seeing as it's Her Highness asking, let's give it all we've got, {NICKNAME}.

subQuests.subQuestName: Continue onward through the Cave of Eerie Murmurs
Continue onward through the Cave of Eerie Murmurs

790670301.text: It's so chilly around here... Such a strange vibe...

790670302.text: Paimon's just glad we haven't seen anything weird...

790670303.text: ...Wait a sec, what's that carved on the wall over there?

790670306.text: "...After setting up the trial herself, the princess awaited her Guardian within the kingdom..."

790670307.text: I think I recall this story from the kingdom's records.

790670308.text: In the legend, it is said that despite the passing of much time, still there came no sign of a Guardian, and it seemed that the kingdom's resources would soon run dry. The princess, whose name was Ceoya, therefore made a decision...

790670309.text: She let the kingdom's people fall into a deep slumber and sealed off all its land except the tower, where she alone remained to await the coming of the Guardian...

790670311.text: The Guardian that she awaited never came. In the end, she is said to have come to the Cave of Eerie Murmurs alone, then vanished from the world without a trace...

790670312.text: It is true that this princess showed great courage, but I cannot say that I agree with her approach.

790670313.text: As I see it, by deciding to simply wait there while her people slept in blissful ignorance, she consigned her kingdom to an unknown fate.

790670314.text: Instead, she should have taken the initiative by calling upon her people to unite as one, seeking out this Guardian together.

790670315.text: ...If she had done this, even if all their efforts had turned out to be in vain, at least she would have known that she'd done all she could.

790670316.text: Heh, it's just as the last line of the story says: "Stories follow rules, unfolding in cyclical patterns, but each should follow its own course."

790670317.text: Your Highness, it hasn't come to that yet...

790670318.text: Yeah, c'mon, there's still hope! And who knows, there might be some important clues left for us to find!

790670319.text: Forgive me, I seem to have gotten a little carried away... Anyway, let's keep searching.

790670320.text: Looking around, it seems like we haven't completed the trials in the Cave of Eerie Murmurs yet...

subQuests.subQuestName: Continue onward through the Cave of Eerie Murmurs
Continue onward through the Cave of Eerie Murmurs
Try to complete the trial in the Cave of Eerie Murmurs

790670601.text: Oh, my leg... Is it still on the ground? I can barely feel it anymore.

790670604.text: ...Those princesses from the past, they seem to have left, too. I hope that they'll never return to the Cave of Eerie Murmurs.

790670605.text: Hehe, seems our trip to the Cave of Eerie Murmurs wasn't for nothing after all. With the relic lit up, there's hope for Your Highness's kingdom again.

790670606.text: That is indeed so. The fact that the relic has lit up means that it has found a "Guardian" worthy of acknowledgment.

790670607.text: It seems the "Guardian" that the relic was looking for was not a valiant warrior in the usual sense.

790670608.text: A true "Guardian" who is worthy of acknowledgment is one who always follows their heart; someone who pushes forward relentlessly, in spite of their fear.

790670609.text: It turns out that this relic, which we'd been treating like the problem, was actually the answer all along.

790670610.text: Those manuscripts that were waiting in the cave...

790670611.text: They've been waiting for their path to appear... Waiting all this time.

790670612.text: But waiting leads only to more waiting. Hehe, no one can find the solution to a problem simply by searching within the problem itself.

790670613.text: Like... You wouldn't be able to pick a leaf from a tree if you were standing on the leaf itself.

790670614.text: Uhh... Sounds complicated. Paimon's feeling dizzy now...

790670615.text: Anyway, none of them were acknowledged by the relic as Guardians. Your Highness and Mr. Faurobert were though!

790670616.text: So now the relic has lit up and we've found our Guardian, doesn't that mean that the problem's solved, Your Highness?

790670617.text: Well, you could say that. But I still haven't managed to figure out exactly why it lit up. Looks like Saborn and Souffache will be doing some more research for me.

790670618.text: Oh, and now that the Guardian's been chosen, doesn't that mean that the relic's trial has lost its meaning, too?

subQuests.subQuestName: Try to complete the trial in the Cave of Eerie Murmurs

790671201.text: Yay! That must mean we've passed this trial, huh? Hehe, that all went pretty smoothly.

790671204.text: You're in such good shape! *sigh* If only I was as talented as you are...

790671206.text: "Stories follow rules, unfolding in cyclical patterns, but each should follow its own course."

790671207.text: "Once upon a time, there was a paper frog who wished he had a pair of wings."

790671208.text: "He prayed to the goddess, who told him that if he could jump higher than all the other frogs, he would have his wings..."

790671209.text: "Long ago, there was a princess who personally set up a trial in the kingdom..."

790671210.text: "She waited, and waited, and waited. O Guardian, where art thou..."

subQuests.subQuestName: Try to complete the trial in the Cave of Eerie Murmurs
Try to complete the trial in the Cave of Eerie Murmurs

790670501.text: Well, seems like we've passed all the trials, right?

790670541.text: ...I brought the relic, but it hasn't reacted at all.

790670504.text: Are we really meant to just keep waiting here? But... What exactly are we waiting for?

790670505.text: It's not like some kind of god's gonna suddenly swoop down and tell us what to do, is it?

790670506.text: What we are willing to do... is wait. All we can do... is wait.

790670507.text: Meaning lies in waiting; the future lies unknown.

790670508.text: When did they appear? And insisting that we wait like that... What are we even waiting for!?

790670509.text: Perhaps they do not know either. Which is why...

Leave the Cave of Eerie Murmurs
Leave the Cave of Eerie Murmurs

790670701.text: Honorable Guardian, what can I do for you?

790670702.text: About the kingdoms that failed to fulfill their calling...

790670703.text: You... Alright. Since the Princess herself has acknowledged you as the "Paladin of Breezes and Bells," it is only right that I tell you about such matters.

790670704.text: Prior to the current era of the Kingdom of Breezes and Bells, this land has known many kingdoms.

790670705.text: Just like us, their "calling" was to find a "Guardian of the Kingdom" who would be acknowledged by the relic.

790670706.text: But these kingdoms, which were established to fulfill a "calling," declined and vanished before they could fulfill it.

790670707.text: Not a single one of them managed to find a Guardian who could save the whole kingdom.

790670709.text: So... If you can't fulfill this "calling" of yours, something bad will happen?

790670710.text: That is correct. In some cases, the subjects of the kingdom suddenly lost their voices, while in others, the kingdom's water supply dried up overnight...

790670711.text: Having lost their "future," all of these kingdoms eventually faded into oblivion.

790670712.text: If we cannot fulfill our "calling"... this will be our fate too.

790670713.text: ...In any case, I wish you good luck, Paladin.

790671101.text: Oh! Pleasure to meet you, hahaha! It seems you're a popular one indeed — even Her Highness Princess Cimest knows of you!

790671103.text: Oh... Such a heavy topic. Well, seeing as you've asked, it would be rude not to give you an answer.

790671104.text: Oh, but... Everything seems fine over at Rainsong Pond? You all look so happy to be jumping around and taking part in the contest...

790671105.text: In one sense, that is so. The waters of Rainsong Pond have never dried up, and the contest has never been interrupted.

790671106.text: Each committee working tirelessly away, and each contestant training constantly, doing everything they can to be up to the task of saving the princess someday.

790671107.text: But all those paper frogs, endlessly laboring... They are the "price" that Rainsong Pond has paid.

790671108.text: From the moment we are born, our "calling" is to practice jumping and save the princess... Every aspect of life at Rainsong Pond revolves around this.

790671109.text: Innumerable paper frogs have sat on Rainsong Pond's committee, and countless champions have been chosen... But all this time, we've never managed to find our princess.

790671110.text: Generation upon generation of frustrated champions have thus aged away, not knowing how to fulfill the "calling" that they so cherished...

790671111.text: All they can do is watch helplessly as their once powerful legs grow weak and their fine webbed feet gradually wither away.

790671112.text: Ha... And worst of all, because our champions keep aging, we must constantly train new ones to ensure that we have the strongest paper frogs ready at all times should the princess suddenly appear.

790671113.text: So Rainsong Pond's contest continues without any sign of an ending. Yet now, none remember the names of those champions who — though they too once cherished the calling — ended up aging away in helpless impotence.

790671114.text: As Princess Cimest put it, weighed down by the burden of unrealized ambition, they are left with no other choice but to end their days in obscurity. Such a fate is crueler than the fall of a kingdom.

790671115.text: But that's enough about all that! The atmosphere's suddenly feeling rather heavy. Let us place our trust in Faurobert and Princess Cimest — I'm sure they'll be able to do something about it.

790671117.text: Oh, that good fellow? He said he was going for a stroll to get some fresh air. Perhaps he's practicing his diving as we speak.

790671118.text: *sigh* If only Estampe could share some of his relaxed mindset with Faurobert. Even a fifth of it would do...

790671120.text: Alright, please take care. I'll be waiting here for you all to return.

790679911.text: [Timeline: The relic lights up, the current takes form, the lamp flies in, the player walks over to the current]
